app_info.subtitle: Shared, verifiable AI memory
app_info.description: emem is a shared, verifiable memory of the physical world for AI. Every place resolves to one canonical address, every observation about it becomes one signed fact you can verify offline, and every fact has a short citation token that resolves anywhere to the byte-identical signed value. Ask about a place (elevation, vegetation, surface water, built-up context, flood signals), an area (a native-resolution raster field, or a field over time), change over time, or similarity between places; get back cite-able, ed25519-signed receipts. No API key or signup required.

justifications.read_only_justification: Grounds the question against real places and, on a cold cell, auto-materializes and signs new facts (Sentinel-2/-1, Cop-DEM, JRC GSW, Overture, weather) into emem's publicly readable store before answering. Nothing is overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint stays false, but the call can add state that other readers will see and therefore is not read-only.
justifications.open_world_justification: This tool resolves real-world place mentions and may fetch upstream Earth-observation data to answer the user's place-based question. It does not create public content or affect external systems. This flag answers MCP's question, which is whether the call may reach an unbounded set of external entities (here: upstream Earth-observation archives), not whether it writes anything. This flag is not about writing. What this call CAN add is stated in readOnlyHint_justification beside it: on a cold cell it materialises and signs new facts into emem's publicly readable store, which is why readOnlyHint is false here. Nothing is overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint is false. Nine of the sixteen tools in this submission are strictly read-only. This one is among the other seven that can add state. None of the nine exposes any of emem's write verbs, and nothing a user sends is written: what materialises is derived from public Earth-observation sources.
justifications.destructive_justification: This tool is read-only. It does not delete or modify any data.

justifications.read_only_justification: Resolves a place name to coordinates and available bands. No writes.
justifications.open_world_justification: Corrected 2026-08-27 on a reviewer's reading, and they were right. This tool RESOLVES a place name to a canonical cell64 and reports what is held there. Resolution consults a local gazetteer first and can fall through to public OSM geocoders, but it only reads them: nothing is posted, published, sent or created, and no state outside this responder changes. Under the review guideline -- openWorldHint is true when a call can WRITE TO or CHANGE publicly visible internet state -- that is false. We had it true on the MCP specification's broader reading, where the flag asks whether a tool may interact with an open world of external entities at all. Both readings are defensible; the directory's is the one that governs here.

justifications.read_only_justification: Recall auto-materializes on a miss: if the requested band is not yet held for that cell, the responder fetches it upstream, signs the resulting fact and appends it to the shared store. Append-only, never an overwrite, so destructiveHint stays false.
justifications.open_world_justification: This tool can auto-materialize facts from registered Earth-observation data sources when a requested band is missing. This flag answers MCP's question, which is whether the call may reach an unbounded set of external entities (here: upstream Earth-observation archives), not whether it writes anything. This flag is not about writing. What this call CAN add is stated in readOnlyHint_justification beside it: on a cold cell it materialises and signs new facts into emem's publicly readable store, which is why readOnlyHint is false here. Nothing is overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint is false. Nine of the sixteen tools in this submission are strictly read-only. This one is among the other seven that can add state. None of the nine exposes any of emem's write verbs, and nothing a user sends is written: what materialises is derived from public Earth-observation sources.

justifications.read_only_justification: Verifies a signed receipt envelope. No writes.
justifications.open_world_justification: Checks receipt data supplied by the caller without contacting external systems.

justifications.read_only_justification: Composes a citation handle from a cell and fact id. No writes.
justifications.open_world_justification: Formats an address string from data already in hand; contacts nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Corrected 2026-08-27 on a reviewer's reading, and they were right. The search itself writes nothing, but the handler is find_similar_with_auto_materialize: when the query cell has no vector fact, it triggers the materializer for that band and the result is signed and persisted into emem's publicly readable store. That is state a later caller can observe, so readOnlyHint is false. The previous value said "No writes" and the openWorldHint justification beside it already admitted the materialisation, which is two statements about one behaviour with only one of them checked.
justifications.open_world_justification: May materialize an embedding for the seed cell from Earth-observation data before the search. This flag answers MCP's question, which is whether the call may reach an unbounded set of external entities (here: upstream Earth-observation archives), not whether it writes anything. What this call CAN add is stated in readOnlyHint_justification beside it: the materialised embedding is signed and persisted, which is why readOnlyHint is false here. Nothing is overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint is false. Nine of the sixteen tools in this submission are strictly read-only (emem_locate, emem_verify_receipt, emem_memory_token); this one is among the other six, and none of the nine exposes any of emem's write verbs.

justifications.read_only_justification: Compares a value you are about to emit against the signed fact your citation points at and reports the drift. Reads one stored fact; writes nothing. Nine of the sixteen tools in this submission are strictly read-only, including this one. The other seven can add state by materialising and signing new facts, or by minting an identity; each says so in its own readOnlyHint_justification. Nothing is ever overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint is false everywhere.
justifications.open_world_justification: Checks a value against a fact this responder already holds. Contacts nothing external.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is overwritten or removed; every write is additive and content-addressed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Ranks existing canonical objects against a phrasing so two agents converge on one identity. Reads the entity registry; mints nothing. Nine of the sixteen tools in this submission are strictly read-only, including this one. The other seven can add state by materialising and signing new facts, or by minting an identity; each says so in its own readOnlyHint_justification. Nothing is ever overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint is false everywhere.
justifications.open_world_justification: Searches identities this responder already holds. No upstream call.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is overwritten or removed; every write is additive and content-addressed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reports where independently signed facts disagree for the same place, band and time. A read over the corpus; it records no verdict. Nine of the sixteen tools in this submission are strictly read-only, including this one. The other seven can add state by materialising and signing new facts, or by minting an identity; each says so in its own readOnlyHint_justification. Nothing is ever overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint is false everywhere.
justifications.open_world_justification: Scans facts this responder already holds. Contacts nothing external.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is overwritten or removed; every write is additive and content-addressed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Parses an emem:fact: handle and returns the signed body it cites. Dereference only; writes nothing. Nine of the sixteen tools in this submission are strictly read-only, including this one. The other seven can add state by materialising and signing new facts, or by minting an identity; each says so in its own readOnlyHint_justification. Nothing is ever overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint is false everywhere.
justifications.open_world_justification: Resolves against local storage. A handle that does not resolve here is reported as such rather than fetched from elsewhere.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is overwritten or removed; every write is additive and content-addressed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns the catalogue of emem's own tool surface. Writes nothing. Nine of the sixteen tools in this submission are strictly read-only, including this one. The other seven can add state by materialising and signing new facts, or by minting an identity; each says so in its own readOnlyHint_justification. Nothing is ever overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint is false everywhere.
justifications.open_world_justification: Describes this responder to itself. No external call.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is overwritten or removed; every write is additive and content-addressed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Resolves the emem: citations in a transcript against stored facts and answers allow or deny. Records no verdict and changes nothing. Nine of the sixteen tools in this submission are strictly read-only, including this one. The other seven can add state by materialising and signing new facts, or by minting an identity; each says so in its own readOnlyHint_justification. Nothing is ever overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint is false everywhere.
justifications.open_world_justification: Corrected 2026-08-27 on a reviewer's reading. guard_resolve_token calls storage.get_facts_many and nothing else: no fetch, no materialise, no HTTP. It evaluates against what this responder already holds, which is also why a citation it does not hold is never a denial.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is overwritten or removed; every write is additive and content-addressed.

justifications.read_only_justification: MINTS a shared identity for a real-world object and signs a receipt, so this writes to the SHARED address space that every other agent resolves names against. It is gated: without a valid ed25519 attester block it refuses with 403 and names the missing field. A ChatGPT user has no such key, so in this app it declines rather than writes. Nine of the sixteen tools in this submission are strictly read-only. This one is among the other seven that can add state. Nothing is overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint is false.
justifications.open_world_justification: Resolving the object may reach the geocoding ladder, whose last layer is public OSM services.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is overwritten or removed; every write is additive and content-addressed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Records a SIGNED equivalence between a phrasing or external id and an existing object, changing what every other agent resolves that phrasing to. Same shared address space and the same enlistment gate as emem_entity: unsigned callers get a 403 naming the missing attester. Nine of the sixteen tools in this submission are strictly read-only. This one is among the other seven that can add state. Nothing is overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint is false.
justifications.open_world_justification: May consult external id namespaces (GERS, OSM, Wikidata) while binding.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is overwritten or removed; every write is additive and content-addressed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Dispatches to whichever primitive answers the stated intent, and some of those materialise and sign new facts on a cold cell. It is false here because the union of what it can reach is not read-only, not because the dispatcher itself writes. Nine of the sixteen tools in this submission are strictly read-only. This one is among the other seven that can add state. Nothing is overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint is false.
justifications.open_world_justification: Whatever primitive it selects may reach upstream Earth-observation archives.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is overwritten or removed; every write is additive and content-addressed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Runs each triple through the auto-materialize recall path, so a cold cell is materialised and signed, and the composed bundle is itself persisted so it can be resolved later by token. Nine of the sixteen tools in this submission are strictly read-only. This one is among the other seven that can add state. Nothing is overwritten or removed, so destructiveHint is false.
justifications.open_world_justification: Materialising a cold triple reads upstream Earth-observation sources.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is overwritten or removed; every write is additive and content-addressed.

test_cases.description: Resolves the airport to one canonical cell64 and returns the elevation there as a signed fact with its content id and an ed25519 receipt.
test_cases.user_prompt: What is the elevation at Helsinki-Vantaa Airport?
test_cases.expected_output: Resolves the airport to one canonical cell64 and returns the elevation there as a signed fact with its content id and an ed25519 receipt.

test_cases.description: Returns the bands held at that cell with their values, each as a signed fact, and names the bands it does not hold rather than implying none exist.
test_cases.user_prompt: What signed facts are available for Lake Erie, Ohio?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the bands held at that cell with their values, each as a signed fact, and names the bands it does not hold rather than implying none exist.

test_cases.description: Returns an emem:fact: token of the form emem:fact:<cell64>:<fact_cid>, about 84 characters, which resolves to the byte-identical signed reading in any later session.
test_cases.user_prompt: Give me a citation token for the NDVI at this farm that I can re-verify later.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns an emem:fact: token of the form emem:fact:<cell64>:<fact_cid>, about 84 characters, which resolves to the byte-identical signed reading in any later session.

test_cases.description: Dereferences the token to the signed body it cites and checks the ed25519 receipt against the responder's published key, so the answer does not depend on trusting whoever sent it.
test_cases.user_prompt: Someone handed me an emem:fact: token. Is it genuine, and what does it say?
test_cases.expected_output: Dereferences the token to the signed body it cites and checks the ed25519 receipt against the responder's published key, so the answer does not depend on trusting whoever sent it.

test_cases.description: Reports where independently signed facts differ for the same place, band and time, with a severity score, or states plainly that no disagreement is held.
test_cases.user_prompt: Do any sources disagree about the vegetation index at this place?
test_cases.expected_output: Reports where independently signed facts differ for the same place, band and time, with a severity score, or states plainly that no disagreement is held.
